newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Riots rock Zambian capital after fire guts market.
newsitem.headline: Riots rock Zambian capital after fire guts market.

text.p: Scores of market traders rioted in the Zambian capital on Wednesday, for the second time this week, after a mysterious fire gutted their sprawling market near the city centre on Tuesday night.
Police fired teargas and beat suspected rioters after angry youths vandalised property in the central business district.
By mid-morning the area was deserted as apprehensive traders closed shops and residents abandoned the city centre. Armed police patrolled the empty streets, ordering people to leave or face arrest.
On Monday scores of youths looted shops and besieged the presidential palace after police burnt their wooden vending stalls in an effort by local authorities to clean up the city.
President Frederick Chiluba subsequently assured the vendors they had his support to rebuild their stalls.
But police fighting the rioters on Wednesday destroyed more stalls, sparking outrage from the vendors.
Local authorities have stepped up a campaign against illegal vending following the opening of a new market in the city on Saturday.
The market, built with Israeli government help, has room for only 3,000 of the more than 10,000 vendors in the city.

Tuesday night's fire is the second to have destroyed public property this week, following a blaze which damaged the first floor of a government building housing vice president Godfrey Miyanda's office.
Police said they were still investigating the cause of both fires.
